A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantially revised objective, both PDFs develop the same appearance, motion, and geometry framework using SVD-generated training videos. The text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary Sections H–N.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection accuracies, modality ablations, and qualitative Grad-CAM analyses in Tables 2–3 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, human studies, generator evaluations, detection results, and ablations in the main paper and supplement.

M1.justification: v1 combines separately trained classifiers through weighted logit ensembling. v2 introduces a nearest-real-feature contrastive loss and a learned fusion network that concatenates modality features before further convolutional processing (Section 4.2; Appendix J). Appendix H.2 also introduces artifact refinement using localized masks and multiview inpainting. These are procedural changes beyond renaming the framework L3DE.

E1.justification: The Pexels/SVD training sources remain, but evaluation expands substantially. v1 evaluates Sora, Pika, and Runway-Gen2 against real videos including Pixabay. v2 evaluates newer generator coverage including Kling, MiniMax, Vidu, Luma, CogVideoX, and Runway-Gen3, and adds static/dynamic reconstruction datasets, ECTV quality evaluation, and video refinement. Pika, Runway-Gen2, and Pixabay are absent from the revised evaluations.

E2.justification: CNNDetection and DIRE remain detection comparators, with NPR added in Table A6. The new quality-evaluation comparisons actually evaluate selected VBench metrics and EvalCrafter against L3DE (Table 4), with another EvalCrafter comparison on ECTV (Table A9). This substantially broadens the comparison methods beyond v1's two image detectors.

E3.justification: Training grows from 6,946 real and 6,946 synthetic videos to 80,000 of each. v2 introduces matched-prompt generator evaluation, reconstruction protocols using 3D-GS/SC-GS and PSNR, selection for successful pose estimation, and human studies including 15 participants rating 300 videos. Accuracy is supplemented by reconstruction and human-agreement metrics. The stated learning rate and batch size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the original pairwise modality-ensemble ablation with contrastive-loss and addition-versus-concatenation experiments (Table A8). It adds controlled training-diversity analyses for motion and indoor/outdoor scenes (Table A7), quantitative validation of localized artifacts against reconstruction errors and human annotations, and refinement examples. Some qualitative failure motifs recur, but the analytical evidence expands substantially.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's accuracy summaries, v2 introduces Spearman rank-correlation estimation for agreement with reconstruction quality, human ratings, and annotated regions (Tables 2–4; Figure 5). This adds statistical association analysis, but neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the original detection results and adds extensive validation, ablation, and generator-ranking results. New findings include fusion correlations of 0.7566 with reconstruction quality (Table 2) and 0.6484 with human ratings (Figure 5). Sora detection is reported as 81.33% in v1 Table 3 and 56.31% in v2 Table A6, but changed methods, training data, and test sets prevent interpreting this as a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's weighted-logit equation, v2 introduces mathematical definitions for the contrastive objective, clipped reconstruction-quality deficit, and simulation gap G = 1 − S (Equations 1–5). These are limited formal additions supporting the method and evaluation; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from detecting generated videos and explaining transferable artifacts to providing an interpretable, quantitative measure of 3D visual coherence. v2 adds core claims of alignment with reconstruction quality and human judgment, generator benchmarking, and synthesis refinement. Fake-video detection becomes a downstream application rather than the principal objective.

C2.justification: v2 interprets classifier confidence as a coherence measure and fusion as capturing more complex inconsistencies. It adds substantive qualifications concerning reconstruction-selection constraints, training-data diversity, and the distinction between visual coherence and comprehensive physical simulation (Appendices M–N). v1 primarily discusses future-generator generalization and limited video length; the latter limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantially fuller reproducibility information: scene-cut processing, cropping and resizing instructions, specific feature-extractor variants, network layers and channel counts, and participant screening and rating rubrics (Appendices I–K; Figure A10). Hardware assignments also change: v1 trains classifiers on 4090 GPUs, whereas v2 reports A100 training and 4090 reconstruction. These disclosures go well beyond v1's brief implementation paragraph.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts from generated-image detection toward video-quality assessment and 3D reconstruction. v2 adds substantive discussion and citations for EvalCrafter, NeRF/Gaussian-splatting reconstruction, and newer generators, while removing the main related-work subsection devoted to generated-image detection. Retained detector citations still support the supplementary detection comparison.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around L3DE. Data curation, method design, validation, and applications become distinct main sections, while detection, implementation details, and limitations are organized in the supplement. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column presentation to a two-column layout with a new opening overview, reconstruction panels, correlation plots, expanded tables, and detailed architecture diagrams. Qualitative examples are reorganized into reference-frame, artifact-region, and Grad-CAM comparisons in the supplement. Some imagery recurs, but the displays and overall layout are extensively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v1 largely supports its realism interpretation through detection accuracy and selected Grad-CAM examples. v2 adds reconstruction and human-study validation of both scores and localized artifacts, controlled ablations, and substantially fuller implementation documentation. These additions materially strengthen evidence for what the method measures, while Appendix M clarifies its scope. Reconstruction validation remains restricted to successfully reconstructed videos and statistical uncertainty is unreported, but the combined validation provides a substantial net improvement.
